corpus_item: RI-QST03 §C ('lockout must be LEGIBLE: a locked faction's members still speak one line explaining why they will not deal with the player') and §B ('explain() renders it as numbers the player can read BEFORE they fail')
why: game/src/sim/quest/gate.js already computes the whole four-part statement with the player's
own numbers in it, and QuestEngine.open() already refuses on it. What it returned was
`the_drowned_court rank 0/2` — a debug string, joined with semicolons, which is a greyed-out
row wearing a sentence's clothes. RI-QST03 scores that as silent lockout in both directions.
So the numbers stay exactly where they are — this file NEVER states a threshold — and the
recruiter is given words to put them in. `{need}` and `{have}` are filled from
FactionGates.evaluate(), which reads faction-gates.json. If a rank demand changes, every line
here changes with it and none of them has to be edited. A line that restated a number would
be a second ladder, and this project has already shipped two ladders for one body.
Order of speaking is fixed and is the order gate.js emits the terms: reputation first
(they do not know you), then attribute (you are not made for it), then the two skills (you
cannot do the work), then world state (the thing has not happened yet). A recruiter says ONE
of these — the first unmet — because a person who lists four reasons is reading a form.

placeholders.{need}: the number the rank demands, from faction-gates.json
placeholders.{have}: the number the player has now
placeholders.{skill}: the display name of the favoured skill the player is closest on
placeholders.{skills}: the faction's favoured skills, as a spoken list
placeholders.{attr}: the display name of the favoured attribute the player is best in
placeholders.{rank}: the name of the rank being refused
placeholders.{rival}: The faction (or factions) whose membership closed this door, from QuestEngine’s own lockedReason. Only ever appears in `rivalry_locked`.

the_rootkeepers.speaker_note: Jeen at the Helstrom undertemple. A keeper does not recruit; she gives you something to count and you either counted it or you did not.
the_rootkeepers.reputation: The slate has {have} beside your name and a Leaf has {need}. That is not a rule I made and I cannot rub it out. Go and do some counting.
the_rootkeepers.attribute: {attr} of {have}. A keeper stands in cold water for a whole day and writes the same number three times to be sure of it, and you would be asleep by the second. Come back at {need}.
the_rootkeepers.skill_1: You have {skill} at {have} and the work wants {need}. I'm not being unkind. A well you count badly is worse to me than a well nobody counted, because I would believe you.
the_rootkeepers.skill_2: One hand is enough for a Leaf and you don't have the second yet. {skill} at {have}, and {need} before I put you on anything that matters.
the_rootkeepers.world_state: Not until {rank} has something to keep, and it hasn't. You know that as well as I do.
the_rootkeepers.welcome: You're on the slate. That's the whole ceremony, and it's the only thing the Rootkeepers own.
the_rootkeepers.rivalry_locked: You keep {rival}, and a keeper keeps one thing. I’m not angry about it. I just can’t write you on the slate twice.

the_ixtu_vakh.speaker_note: Neeth over the sap-house. The cutters are hated and well paid and he assumes you already know both.
the_ixtu_vakh.reputation: I've heard your name {have} times and I want {need}. Nobody starts here. Go and be useful where somebody's watching.
the_ixtu_vakh.attribute: {attr} at {have}? The east track is four days of wet ground and a keeper on the end of it. Bring me {need} and we'll talk.
the_ixtu_vakh.skill_1: {skill} at {have}. The road wants {need} and the road doesn't care that you'd like the money. I've buried two who thought otherwise.
the_ixtu_vakh.skill_2: You can carry, I'll grant you that. The second thing — {skill}, {have}, and I want {need} — is what gets you back again.
the_ixtu_vakh.world_state: {rank} isn't mine to hand out. That's the well's business, and the well hasn't said.
the_ixtu_vakh.welcome: You're written down. There's no oath and no drink. The list is the list.
the_ixtu_vakh.rivalry_locked: You’re on {rival}’s list. A cutter can only be on one, and it isn’t because we’re proud — it’s because they’d know.

the_drowned_court.speaker_note: Vaskh in the burning yard. Everything he says is levelled by the fact that he does this all day.
the_drowned_court.reputation: The tally has you at {have}. Knee-Deep is {need}. You'll get there or you won't, and either way the bay keeps sending them.
the_drowned_court.attribute: {attr} at {have}. A man goes into the water after a body and comes back with it, or he goes in and we fetch two. {need}, and not before.
the_drowned_court.skill_1: {skill} at {have}, and the Court asks {need}. It isn't a test. It's the number at which people stop drowning next to me.
the_drowned_court.skill_2: You can lift. The other half is reading what a body has to say, and {skill} at {have} reads nothing. {need}.
the_drowned_court.world_state: {rank} is a chair, and the chair is occupied. Ask me again when it isn't.
the_drowned_court.welcome: You're in the tally. Everyone gets in it eventually. You've just done it standing up.
the_drowned_court.rivalry_locked: You came in with {rival} on you. The tally doesn’t take people twice and it doesn’t argue about why.

the_dockhands.speaker_note: Eeja at the foot of the crane. There is no institution here at all; there is a board with chalk on it.
the_dockhands.reputation: The board doesn't know you. {have} against {need}, and the hands put the names up, not me.
the_dockhands.attribute: {attr} at {have} and the crate is the crate. Eleven gold a week and the crane takes a finger off a man every winter. {need}, or the winter takes yours.
the_dockhands.skill_1: {skill} at {have}. The board rate is for {need}, and if I chalk you up under it the four who carry your end will rub it off by noon.
the_dockhands.skill_2: You'll do for the lifting. {skill} at {have} is the bit that keeps you off the wrong side of the crane, and I want {need}.
the_dockhands.world_state: {rank} goes to whoever the hands say, when they say it. I don't hold that chalk.
the_dockhands.welcome: Your name's on the board. It stays there until the rain gets in or the hands rub it off.
the_dockhands.rivalry_locked: You work for {rival}. The board’s got one name for one pair of hands, and yours is spoken for.

the_wet_ledger.speaker_note: Belliene on the counting floor. She prices the refusal the way she prices everything.
the_wet_ledger.reputation: The margin has your name in it {have} times and the next line wants {need}. The Ledger remembers people by the margin. Give it more to remember.
the_wet_ledger.attribute: {attr} at {have}. It's a long road to Archon and the fords are the fords. {need}.
the_wet_ledger.skill_1: {skill} at {have}, and I need {need}. I'm not asking you to be clever. I'm asking you to be the sort of clever that doesn't leave a paper trail.
the_wet_ledger.skill_2: The second column is short. {skill} at {have}, {need} wanted, and the difference is what the Ledger pays for.
the_wet_ledger.world_state: {rank} sits at the table and the table is full. Something has to move first, and it won't be me.
the_wet_ledger.welcome: Your name's in the margin. That's how the Ledger remembers people.
the_wet_ledger.rivalry_locked: You are carried by {rival}. A name in two margins is a name in neither, and the Ledger has priced that before.

the_imperial_assize.speaker_note: The Assize is a court and it refuses in the passive, because a court is never the one refusing.
the_imperial_assize.reputation: The roll records {have} against your name and the grade requires {need}. Applications are considered when the roll supports them.
the_imperial_assize.attribute: {attr} is entered at {have} and the grade is set at {need}. The Office does not vary an entry on request.
the_imperial_assize.skill_1: {skill} stands at {have}. The schedule for this grade is {need}. You may sit it again when you have the difference.
the_imperial_assize.skill_2: A second competence is required and yours is entered at {have} against {need}. The clerk will note the application and the shortfall.
the_imperial_assize.world_state: {rank} is filled by vacancy, not by application. There is no vacancy.
the_imperial_assize.welcome: The roll is amended. You are an officer of this court, which is a heavier thing than it sounds.
the_imperial_assize.rivalry_locked: The court is aware of your standing with {rival}. It is not an accusation and it is not appealable. The roll will not be amended.

the_xul_aneekh.speaker_note: The hollow speaks in the plural and does not explain itself twice.
the_xul_aneekh.reputation: You are {have} to the hollow and the name you are asking for is {need}. Names are not given. They are noticed.
the_xul_aneekh.attribute: {attr}, {have}. The deep marsh does not adjust itself to a person. {need}.
the_xul_aneekh.skill_1: {skill} at {have}. We ask {need} of anyone who walks where you are asking to walk, and the ones who went short are still out there.
the_xul_aneekh.skill_2: The second thing is thin. {skill} at {have}, and {need} before the hollow hears you.
the_xul_aneekh.world_state: {rank} is a thing the hollow decides, and the hollow has not spoken.
the_xul_aneekh.welcome: The hollow has a name for you now. You will not like all of what comes with it.
the_xul_aneekh.rivalry_locked: You have already been named, by {rival}. The hollow does not name a thing twice and will not be asked to.

unknown_faction: I don't speak for them and neither does anyone you'll meet on this road.

not_joinable.house_dres: House Dres does not take Argonians and does not take you. They buy; they do not hire.
not_joinable.shadowscale_order: The ku-vastei are not a guild. You do not join one. You send for one, and you pay, and you had better be sure.
not_joinable.deep_kin: That is the hollow's own name for itself. It is the same people and the same door.
not_joinable._note: RI-QST03 §C: a lockout must be legible. These three carry ladders or ids in the build and are joinable by nobody, and FACTION-ROSTER-DESIGN.md §2/§3 gives the reason for each. A player who asks gets the reason rather than silence.
